# A USD bill paid, through a payment block, from a USD bank whose cost bases
# still have a balance. Refused, for the same reason the HKD-bank shape is.
#
# Nothing is realized here — the bill and the cash are both USD, so the
# settlement crosses no rate — and that is exactly what made this one easy to
# miss: the cross-currency arithmetic returns long before the disposal is
# looked at. The disposal happens all the same. 100.00 USD bought at 1.35 has
# a cost basis and an available balance; spending it has to say which basis it
# comes out of, and a payment block has nowhere to say it.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming `Assets:Bank:USD`, the
# 100.00 USD available on it, and the `txn_guid:` route.
# tests/fixtures/fx_settle_usd_bill_with_usd_cash.txt is that route, and shows
# what the refusal is asking for: `cost_basis_split_guid:` on the bank line.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_spending_what_a_settlement_brought_in.py.
bill "BILL-USD-001"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Parts"
    account: "Expenses:Supplies"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD"
    memo: "Bill BILL-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-25
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    memo: "Payment for BILL-USD-001"
